chrome-devtools-mcp.feature: env() values in get_css_styles: DevTools resolves a declaration's env(name) from this list (CSSMatchedStyles.environmentVariable); without it an env() shows its fallback or stays unresolved. WebKit has no command that lists the UA environment variables
chrome-devtools-mcp.review: fix-i-cssbridge-e2e, 2026-11-26: chrome-devtools-mcp 1.14.0 sends it once per get_css_styles call from the bundled DevTools SDK: CSSMatchedStyles.init (out/Default/gen/src/third_party/browser.js line 199, column 5509) awaits CSSModel.getEnvironmentVariables (line 194, column 4559), which returns {} when the agent call answers an error (invoke_getEnvironmentVariables returns the error in the response instead of throwing); the endpoint answers 'wasn't found'. With it, TestClientScenarios/chrome-devtools-mcp-features passes every step, get_css_styles included (the winning and [overloaded] declarations of css.html, <style> source lines, a var() value), and so does the WebKitGTK sequence test TestCDPCSSBridgeDevToolsSequenceOnWebKitGTK. Left untranslated on purpose: an empty list would claim that the page has no UA environment variables, which is false on iOS (env(safe-area-inset-*)), while the error gives DevTools the same {} without that claim. A real translation would have to measure each variable in the page (no WIP command lists them).
